key_insight: FCV-PICRN reconstructs flow structures across large unsupervised gaps by combining Fourier features, complex-valued learning, and Navier–Stokes constraints.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support flow diagnostics when sensors or imaging leave critical wake regions unobserved or noisy.
method: Fourier features encode oscillatory and multiscale flow structures.
Complex-valued convolutional residual blocks learn coupled amplitude–phase representations.
Navier–Stokes constraints guide reconstruction of velocity, pressure, and vorticity.
evidence_signal: Tests cover Taylor–Green and cylinder-wake flows at Re=100, three severe gap geometries with Gaussian or speckle noise, robustness to 20% Gaussian noise, and lower errors than a conventional PINN on 2D Kolmogorov turbulence with 5% Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported benchmarks; performance on three-dimensional, higher-Reynolds-number flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
